findings.title: Editorial pages and shop archives overlap
findings.detail: The seven visible menu hubs sit alongside 113 editorial category page records and 135 shop-category records. Nested editorial pages and flat product archives must be reconciled in the migration plan. Preserve the two inventories until URL decisions are approved.

findings.title: The /dresses/ URL serves a Plus size child archive
findings.detail: WordPress registers /dresses/ as the parent of 11 editorial pages, while WooCommerce registers the same URL as a child of Plus size. A live request serves a single-product archive. The main menu links to /all-dresses/.

findings.title: The ten root shop archives currently use noindex
findings.detail: Live checks of all 10 root shop-category URLs returned a noindex directive. Indexability for the new site needs an explicit decision; do not copy these directives across automatically. The sampled nested editorial Summer Dresses page is indexable.

findings.title: The HTML sitemap has a broken Pants & Leggings hub link
findings.detail: The HTML sitemap points to /pants-and-leggings-blog/, which returned HTTP 404. The editorial hub is /pants/ and the shop archive is /trousers-and-leggings/.

findings.title: Three shop roots are absent from the main navigation
findings.detail: Fashion, Outfits & Sets, and Plus size exist in the current product taxonomy. Outfits & Sets has Casual, Going out, Sporty, and Pajama Sets; Plus size has Blouses, Dresses, and Outfits. These are existing taxonomy records, not recommended additions.

findings.title: Two shop categories use the name Black Leggings
findings.detail: Both /black-leggings/ and /black-leggings-trousers-and-leggings/ sit under Pants and Leggings. Compare assignments before consolidating them.

findings.title: Two product categories currently report no products
findings.detail: Animal Print Cardigans and Pussy Bow Blouses report zero products with hide_empty=false. Keep them in the audit, and decide whether they should be populated, redirected, or removed in the new architecture.

sources.name: Homepage navigation and complete category directory

coverageNotes: This inventory covers all publicly returned WordPress category-page records, WooCommerce Store API category terms including empty terms, and WordPress blog categories as of the audit date. It does not include drafts or private CMS records.

WordPress pages were fetched in two pages (100 + 32) and shop categories in two pages (100 + 35). No parent references are missing. All 106 editorial child pages appear in the homepage directory and page sitemap.

Verified means the record and hierarchy were confirmed in a first-party public API or sitemap. An HTTP status is included only for individually requested URLs; other URLs were not each crawled for status, redirects, canonicals, or content.
There are 250 taxonomy/page records but 245 distinct URLs because five paths are registered in both systems. Treat the systems separately when counting pages.

Pagination URLs, sort/filter parameters, and individual products are excluded from category counts. Shop product counts are a source snapshot and may overlap because products can belong to several categories.
Current category records are an audit baseline, not approval to publish every category on the replacement website.
